references.text: Describes the alternative of two turtledoves or two young pigeons for those who cannot afford a lamb, which verse 11 builds upon with an even more affordable option.
The grain offering also consisted of fine flour (sifted), used here as a sin offering for the poor.
The prohibition against leaven in offerings, parallel to the prohibition against oil and incense on the sin offering in verse 11.
Another example of adapting offering rules for the poor, where a tenth of an ephah of fine flour is also mentioned.
The memorial offering (sifted) used in the jealousy offering, also without oil and incense, because it concerns sin.
Basic instructions regarding the sin offering (chattat), which verse 11 refers to.
Paul writes about Christ becoming poor for our sake, a parallel to God's care for the poor in the sacrificial laws.
Jesus recognizes the widow's small gifts as valuable, reflecting the principle that God accepts offerings according to one's ability.
